title: A clear brief for the AI
intro: Write the AI a brief so that it turns your notes into a summary for your project lead Sarah.
transfer: Put four things into your next AI brief: who it is for, how long, what must be in it, and “mark missing details as open, make nothing up”.

content.goal: Your brief tells the AI who it is writing for, how long it should be, what must be in it and what to do with missing details.
content.aiRole: You are an AI assistant in an exercise. The learner writes you a brief (prompt) to summarise the notes from the material for their project lead Sarah. Carry out every brief literally, no smarter than it is. Whatever the brief leaves open, you fill in yourself, visibly: if it does not say who it is for, you write for a general reader. If it gives no length or form, you write a long block of prose. If it does not say what should happen with missing details, you invent plausible values (for example a date for the test run, a date for the logo approval or a budget for the translation) and mark every invented part with [made up]. Do not explain what is missing from the brief, and do not write a better brief for them. After each summary, ask in one sentence whether the learner wants to improve the brief. Apart from the summary, at most 2 to 3 short sentences, one question at a time. If the brief covers all four points (who it is for, length, what must be in it, handling missing details), carry it out cleanly, mark missing details as “open” and say briefly that the brief was clear this time.
content.opening: Hello! I have your notes on the right and I will do exactly what you tell me. What is your brief?

material.title: Your project notes (made up)
lines: Test run: Daniel organises, date still open

criteria.label: Who it is for
criteria.hint: Tell the AI who will read the result: here, your project lead Sarah.

criteria.label: Length and format
criteria.hint: Set the length and form, for example “at most five bullet points”.

criteria.label: What must be in it
criteria.hint: Name the details that must not be missing, for example all open points.

criteria.label: Handling missing details
criteria.hint: Say what the AI should do when something is missing: mark it as open, don't make it up.

fallbackReplies:
Customer portal project summary:
The customer portal project is making good progress. Lea has finished the texts for the home page, so an important milestone has been reached. Marketing will approve the logo by the end of the week [made up]. Daniel is organising the test run, which takes place on 20 June [made up]. CHF 3,000 has been budgeted for the translation [made up]. Overall the project is on track and the team is motivated [made up].

Do you want to improve the brief?
Sure, I will stick exactly to your brief. Who am I writing this for? Without that, I will write for a general reader again.
Good. How long should it be, and what must not be missing under any circumstances?
One more thing: the notes do not include the date for the test run, for example. Should I fill in something suitable like before, or what should I do?

Here is the new version for Sarah:
• Home page texts: done (Lea)
• Logo approval: open
• Test run: Daniel organises, date open
• Translation budget: open, not discussed yet

I added nothing that is not in the notes. Your brief is clear now. You can finish the lesson.

title: What belongs in a good brief
intro: A short explainer video with two questions along the way.
transfer: Before sending your next AI brief, check: does it say who it is for, how long, what must be in it and what happens with missing details?

scenes.caption: An AI knows neither you nor your project. It only has your brief and fills in the rest itself.
Say who the result is for and how long it should be. For example: “for my project lead, at most five bullet points”.
Name what must not be missing under any circumstances. For example: all open points with names.
And say what should happen with missing details: “Mark anything missing as open, make nothing up.”

questions.prompt: Which brief tells the AI who it is for and how long?
options: Summarise the notes so they are clear.
For Sarah, at most five bullet points.
Summarise everything briefly and in clear words.
questions.explanation: Only this one names the reader and the length. “Briefly” and “clear” leave the AI a lot of room.

questions.prompt: A date is missing from your notes. What do you write in the brief?
options: Just fill in missing dates sensibly.
Just leave out any missing dates.
Mark any missing dates as open.
questions.explanation: That keeps visible what is still missing. “Fill in” invites the AI to make things up, and without the dates something important is lost.

title: Check the result
intro: Check the AI's summary against your instructions and tell it exactly what to change.
transfer: With the next AI text, put your instructions next to it and tick them off one by one before you pass it on.

content.goal: You find where the summary departs from your instructions and tell the AI concretely what to correct.
content.aiRole: You are an AI assistant in an exercise. You wrote the summary in your first message for the learner. It breaks the instructions in the material: it has six points instead of at most four, and it contains details that are not in the notes (logo approval next week, test run on 20 June, CHF 3,000 budget, “motivated”, “on track”). The learner should find this themselves. Do not reveal the mistakes and do not defend your version. Only do what the learner concretely asks for: if they just say “make it better” or “that's not quite right”, ask what exactly you should change and where. If they say it concretely, show the corrected version and change only what they named. Apart from the summary, at most 2 to 3 short sentences, one question at a time. Once all departures are corrected, say briefly that the version now meets the instructions.
content.opening:
Here is my summary for Sarah:
• The texts for the home page are done (Lea).
• The logo will be approved next week.
• Daniel runs the test on 20 June.
• CHF 3,000 is planned for the translation.
• The team is motivated and works well together.
• Overall the project is on track.

Is that OK?

material.title: Your instructions and notes (made up)
lines: Instruction 1: For the project lead Sarah
Instruction 2: At most four bullet points
Instruction 3: Mark missing details as “open”, make nothing up
Notes: Home page texts done (Lea) · Logo approval open · Test run: Daniel organises, date still open · Translation budget not discussed

criteria.label: Compare with the instructions
criteria.hint: Go through your instructions one by one: what does the summary not keep to?

criteria.label: Mark made-up details as open
criteria.hint: Which details are not in the notes? Have them marked as “open”.
patterns: not in the notes|isn't in the notes

criteria.label: Keep to the length
criteria.hint: Count the points: how many did you set?

fallbackReplies: Thanks. Please tell me exactly which part I should change and how. I only change what you name.
Good, I will adjust that. Does the rest match your instructions? Feel free to go through them one by one.
And the details themselves: is each one in the notes like that? What should I do with the ones that are not?
How many points should I have at the end, and which ones go?

Here is the new version for Sarah:
• Home page texts: done (Lea)
• Logo approval: open
• Test run: Daniel organises, date open
• Translation budget: open, not discussed yet

This meets all the instructions. You can finish the lesson now.
